ideas.hypothesis: Prices underreact to earnings news, so a name whose results produced a strong positive multi-day reaction keeps drifting in the same direction for weeks.
ideas.rule: Entry: a headline from the last 24h names the company together with results, earnings, record quarter or guidance, AND its d5 move is >= +8%. Buy max shares, horizon 10 trading days, exit at horizon or the -10% stop. At most 1 entry per name per results season.
ideas.source: Bernard & Thomas 1989 (post-earnings-announcement drift); Chan, Jegadeesh & Lakonishok 1996
ideas.note: New today; first trigger IFX.DE (record-quarter headline, d5 +13.21%).

ideas.hypothesis: Investors anchor on recent highs, so stocks at their 3-month high after a strong month underreact to good news and keep rising.
ideas.rule: Entry: below_3m_high >= -1.0% AND d20 >= +10%. Buy max shares of at most the 2 qualifying names with the largest d20, horizon 20 trading days, exit at horizon or the -10% stop.
ideas.source: George & Hwang 2004 (52-week high and momentum), adapted to the 3-month high
ideas.note: New today; qualifiers BAYN.DE (d20 +27.85%), SAN.PA (d20 +22.46%), AZN.L (d20 +12.50%); top 2 bought.

ideas.hypothesis: Large weekly drops without company-specific news are often liquidity or flow driven and partly reverse within a week.
ideas.rule: Entry: d5 <= -7% AND no headline in the input names the company. Buy max shares, horizon 5 trading days, exit at horizon or the -10% stop.
ideas.source: Jegadeesh 1990; Lehmann 1990 (short-term reversal); Chan 2003 (news vs no-news drift/reversal)
ideas.note: New today; first trigger EDV.L (d5 -8.55%, no Endeavour headline).
